stem: A Massachusetts licensure applicant submits an examination application missing the required proof of date and place of birth, together with the full fee. The Board declines to consider the application. He asks whether he will get his fee back. What is the correct position?

choices.text: The fee is refundable because the application was never substantively evaluated.
The fee is refundable on written request within 30 days of the Board's decision.
The fee is held as a credit against his next licensure application.
The fee is refundable only if the omission resulted from the Board's own error.
The fee is non-refundable once the application has been reviewed and acted upon.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 3.01(3) sets out what a completed application must include, and 247 CMR 3.01(8) permits the Board to refuse to consider any application that has not been properly completed. 247 CMR 3.01(9) provides that all fees submitted in connection with a licensure application that is reviewed and acted upon by the Board are non-refundable.

choice_analysis.A: Declining to consider an application is itself acting upon it.
choice_analysis.C: The regulation provides for non-refundability, not carry-forward credit.
choice_analysis.D: The non-refundability provision is not conditioned on fault.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: reviewed and acted upon fees are non-refundable.

related_facts: A name change must be notified in writing to the Board or the Board's designee with the application.
explanation.mpje_trap: Refusing to consider an application is still acting on it, so the fee does not come back.

reasoning_steps: Identify the application as improperly completed
Note the Board's power to refuse to consider it
Apply the non-refundability provision to the fee already submitted
